Social and Economic Impacts
If a conversion plant were to be constructed it is estimated that approximately 2,750 employees would be required during the three year construction period, and 625 employees would be required for the plant's operation. The implications of a conversion scenario have been discussed in a previous section, "Impacts on the Human Environment".
It seems reasonable to assume that conversion would be considered only if accompanied by a reasonably high level of Crow coal development (AF-2) and increasing demand for employment opportunities by Crow people (LFPR-2). Under this set of circumstances total coal associated employment resulting from plant construction and initial operation would be expected to peak at nearly 5300 during the height of construction, dropping abruptly to about 790 immediately following completion of construction and then stabilize at around 1200 between 1992 and 2000. This final employment level would be over 2 1/2 times that derived from the most probable level of Westmoreland mining development (scenario 1) under the same developmental conditions.
Because of the increased operational requirements, Crow Indians would have greater opportunity for employment than under Scenario 1 as Crow employment preference clauses are stipulated in the Amended Leases. It would follow that non-agricultural wage income would rise in direct proportion to the increase in employment, resulting in an increase of more than 2 1/2 times that for Scenario 1. Royalty payments would be expected to be about 11 percent higher than for scenario 1 and other significant incomes from the plant could be expected by the Tribe, depending on the terms of the modified agreement.
